message.content:
The fog rolled in like a gray tide, swallowing the coastline whole. Elias stood at the top of the Iron Point Lighthouse, his hand resting on the cold brass railing. For thirty years, this structure had been his only companion, a stone sentinel against the chaotic sea. The beam swept out in rhythmic pulses, a heartbeat of light piercing the gloom, warning ships of the jagged rocks hidden beneath the churning waves.

Elias loved the solitude, but he also feared it. The silence here was heavy, pressing against his eardrums. He spent his days polishing the lens, trimming the wick, and watching the horizon for any sign of life. Most days, there was nothing. Just the endless gray. But today, a small fishing boat bobbed dangerously close to the shoals. The captain, a young man Elias had never met, was struggling against the current. The light was their only hope, but the fog was thick enough to obscure even the beam’s reflection.

Elias grabbed the radio handset. Static crackled, then died. He shouted into the void, his voice raw and desperate. "Turn left! Hard left!" There was no response. The boat drifted closer to the rocks. Elias felt a surge of panic
